'''Diana Ürge-Vorsatz''' is a Hungarian scientist. She is a vice-chair of the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change, and professor of [[Environmental science|Environmental Sciences]] at [[Central European University]]. She was the Director of the Center for Climate Change and Sustainable Energy Policy. She has published widely on environmental and [[Energy Studies Institute|energy studies]], primarily [[climate change mitigation]].<ref name="Jones">{{cite news |last1=Jones |first1=Nicola |title=For a Scientist and Mother, Climate Change Is Generational 'Robbery' |url=https://e360.yale.edu/features/diana-urge-vorsatz-climate-change |access-date=3 November 2022 |work=Yale E360 |date=September 22, 2022}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://bcsdh.hu/event/business-breakfast-our-guest-speaker-diana-urge-vorsatz/|title=Business Breakfast with Diána Ürge-Vorsatz|website=BCSD Hungary|language=hu|date=22 March 2016|access-date=2019-02-12|archive-date=2019-03-07|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190307173813/https://bcsdh.hu/event/business-breakfast-our-guest-speaker-diana-urge-vorsatz/}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Diana Ürge-Vorsatz |url=https://orcid.org/0000-0003-2570-5341 |website=ORCID |access-date=8 November 2022}}</ref>

Ürge-Vorsatz was a coordinating lead author of both the Fourth and Fifth Assessment Reports ([[IPCC Fourth Assessment Report|AR4]] and [[IPCC Fifth Assessment Report|AR5]]) of the [[Nobel Peace Prize]]-winning [[Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change]].<ref name="VEF"/>

== Early life ==
Diana Ürge-Vorsatz was born in 1968 in [[Berlin]]. She grew up in Budapest, where she attended Radnóti Miklós High School.<ref name="Hu">{{cite web |title=Portré |url=https://m.hvg.hu/360/hetilap360/2017/16/20171620portre1 |publisher=hvg360 |language=hu |access-date=2022-10-06}}</ref>
From 1986 to 1992 Ürge-Vorsatz attended [[Eötvös Loránd University]] (ELTE) in Budapest, earning a master's degree in physics in 1992 with specialization in both [[Astrophysics]] and Environmental Physics.
During this time, Ürge-Vorsatz also studied as a visiting student at [[Brunel University London]] from 1990 to 1991, where she took graduate courses in environmental pollution science and conducted research in environmental physics. In the summer of 1992, following her Master's graduation, Ürge-Vorsatz attended a post-grad program in [[Environmental science|Environmental Science]] at [[Central European University]]. 
<ref name="People"/> She credits her switch in discipline from astrophysics to climate change as coming as an epiphany that occurred during a meeting on an unrelated topic, where she was suddenly struck by a "a strong feeling that she must focus on problems that are happening on Earth."<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Qv8iGxifi1k&t=1063s&ab_channel=YOUNGOScience | title=Climate Café II: IPCC Vice Chair | website=[[YouTube]] | date=10 April 2024 }}</ref>

Ürge-Vorsatz was a [[Fulbright Scholar]] within the Energy and Resources Group at the [[University of California, Los Angeles]] and [[University of California, Berkeley|Berkeley]]. She earned her PhD in [[Environmental Science]] and [[Engineering]] from the University of California in 1996. Her [[dissertation]] is titled "Evaluating US Residential and Commercial Electricity Conservation Potentials: an Analysis of the Lighting Sector."<ref name="SHARE|language=hu">{{cite web |title=Prof. Dr. Diána Ürge-Vorsatz |url=https://share-architects.com/speaker/prof-dr-diana-urge-vorsatz/ |website=SHARE Architects |access-date=4 November 2022}}</ref>

== Career ==
Ürge-Vorsatz became an associate professor at [[Central European University]] (CEU) in 2001, and a full Professor in 2007. Ürge-Vorsatz accepted the position of Director for the Center for Climate Change and Sustainable Energy Policy  (3CSEP) in 2007.<ref>{{cite web |title=Ürge-Vorsatz Diana |url=https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Member/%C3%9Crge-Vorsatz_Diana |website=Academy of Europe |access-date=4 November 2022}}</ref><ref name="People">{{cite web |title=Diana Ürge-Vorsatz |url=https://people.ceu.edu/diana_urge-vorsatz |website=CEU People |access-date=4 November 2022}}</ref>

Ürge-Vorsatz has served on the Scientific Expert Group on Climate Change of the United Nations, and led work on the Global Energy Assessment of buildings.
She is the vice chair of the [[Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change]] Working Group III (WG III).<ref name="WGIII">{{cite web |title=Diana Ürge-Vorsatz |url=https://ec.europa.eu/info/persons/diana-urge-vorsatz_en |website=European Commission - European Commission |access-date=7 November 2022 |language=en}}</ref><ref name="Allen">{{cite news |last1=Allen |first1=Gabe |title=Immediate Action Needed to Mitigate Climate Change, IPCC Says |url=https://www.discovermagazine.com/environment/immediate-action-needed-to-mitigate-climate-change-ipcc-says |access-date=7 November 2022 |work=Discover Magazine |date=April 5, 2022 |language=en}}</ref>

Ürge-Vorsatz has been serving as Vice Chair of the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change since July 2023.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.ipcc.ch/people/diana-urge-vorsatz/ | title=Diana Ürge-Vorsatz — IPCC }}</ref> Ürge-Vorsatz serves on the Board of Directors of  [[Annual Reviews (publisher)|Annual Reviews]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026 |title=Our Team |url=https://www.annualreviews.org/about/our-team |access-date=2026-08-24 |website=Annual Reviews |language=en}}</ref> In 2026, Ürge-Vorsatz became a co-editor of the ''[[Annual Review of Environment and Resources]]''.<ref>{{cite web |title=Annual Review of Environment and Resources, Current Editorial Committee |url=https://www.annualreviews.org/db/directory?0000,energy |website=Annual Reviews Directory |access-date=12 August 2026 |language=en}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
In 1984, Ürge-Vorsatz won the Hungarian National Championship in [[orienteering]].<ref name="CEU">{{Cite web|url=https://people.ceu.edu/diana_urge-vorsatz|title=Diana Ürge-Vorsatz {{!}} CEU People|website=people.ceu.edu|access-date=2019-02-11}}</ref> She is the mother of seven children.
